title: An ensemble approach driven by spatial interaction for modelling urban epidemic dynamics
abstract: Modelling spatial interactions remains a core issue in geographic information science. Faced with the emerging, non-stationary spread of epidemics, the effects and uncertainties of spatial interactions are amplified. Limited by reliance on a single spatial interaction prior, existing models perform well in specific scenarios but suffer from prediction drift across multi-phase epidemics, thereby hindering real-time and dynamic policy adjustments. To address this limitation, we propose an ensemble approach driven by spatial interaction, built upon a foundational metapopulation model. Using the 2022 Shanghai Omicron outbreak as a case study, we evaluated the proposed ensemble model against 14 mechanistic and machine learning baselines. In multi-phase prediction tasks, the proposed ensemble model achieves the best overall performance with mean ranks of 3.25 for RMSE and 4.00 for R2, surpassing all baselines with mean ranks ranging from 5 to 15. Furthermore, it improves mean predictive accuracy by 29% to 72% compared with the non-ensemble models, while reducing the prediction error interval by 10% to 84%. Finally, we generated model-based projections across multiple counterfactual scenarios to explore responses to changes in intervention timing and intensity.

title: A novel satellite embedding-driven SWOT framework for river discharge estimation: a case study of the Yangtze river
abstract: Accurate river discharge estimation is essential for water cycle modeling, water hazards prevention, water ecosystem protection and water resource management. However, conventional ground-based gauging networks are often sparsely distributed and insufficient to capture the complex hydrodynamic characteristics within large and heterogeneous river basins. With the rapid advancement of remote sensing technologies, particularly the launch of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission, new opportunities have emerged for large-scale and continuous river discharge estimation. In this study, we develop and evaluate a SWOT-based river discharge estimation framework for the Yangtze River by integrating SWOT RiverSP hydraulic observations organized on the SWORD river network with Satellite Embedding V1 data in a random forest model to capture both hydrodynamic and geomorphological characteristics. The framework is evaluated using temporally separated training and testing observations from nine gauging stations along the Yangtze River mainstream, with station-specific nonlinear empirical models used for comparison. The main conclusions are as follows: 1) The random forest model substantially improves discharge estimation relative to the empirical formulation, with a maximum NSE gain of 0.4372 and an NRMSE reduction of up to 0.1175; 2) The model demonstrates reliable performance across the nine gauging stations, with all stations achieving NSE ≥ 0.72 and the overall performance reaching NSE = 0.8910 and NRMSE = 0.0664; 3) The spatially explicit discharge estimates show strong agreement with reach-scale results (correlation ≈ 0.9), indicating that water level exerts primary control on discharge, while channel width and geometry significantly modulate discharge responses in morphologically complex reaches. These results demonstrate the potential of combining SWOT hydraulics with satellite foundation embeddings to improve discharge estimation.

title: SegDis: Foreground Segmentation Followed by Type Discrimination for Salient and Camouflaged Object Detection
abstract: Salient and camouflaged object detection (SOD and COD) both recover foreground support, yet most joint methods output only a binary mask and therefore cannot distinguish the type. USC12K distinguishes the two types, but its baseline USCNet still binds foreground existence to the type within a single normalization, so the failure source cannot be attributed. Our cross-task study shows that foreground localization transfers between SOD and COD, whereas type discrimination does not: a COD-only model recovers foreground on SOD images but its type judgement follows the training distribution rather than the foreground-background relation, so the two decisions require separate mechanisms. SegDis factorizes the output into an explicit foreground probability and a conditional type probability given foreground: FLR provides high-quality task-agnostic support, and RTA refines the SOD/COD assignment from the foreground-background relation without a task identifier. Because support is explicit, each ground-truth foreground pixel is classified as correct-type, type-swapped, or missed, so foreground-recovery and type-assignment errors are diagnosed separately. With PVT-v2-B2, SegDis attains 68.98% FG-mIoU and 78.35% mIoU on USC12K at about one-eighth of USCNet's parameters; CSCS is 5.75.

title: Beyond Similarity Entropy: A Rank-Guided Data-Free Quantization Framework for Vision Transformers
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated remarkable performance, yet their computational and memory demands pose significant challenges for deployment on mobile devices. Data-free quantization (DFQ) enables the compression of ViTs without access to their original training data. Existing DFQ methods often synthesize calibration samples by maximizing the entropy of patch similarity. However, similarity entropy describes the dispersion of similarity values without ensuring that the generated samples cover diverse feature directions, potentially limiting their effectiveness for quantization calibration. To address this limitation, we propose RankQ-ViT, a rank-guided DFQ framework for ViTs. We first observe that patch similarity matrices derived from Gaussian noise tend to have lower ranks than those derived from real images. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a block-aware self-contrastive objective that promotes feature diversity during synthetic data generation without explicitly computing matrix rank at each optimization step. We then select calibration samples based on their rank and semantic consistency and use them for block-wise reconstruction of the quantized model. Experiments on ImageNet, COCO, ModelNet40, and ShapeNet demonstrate the effectiveness of RankQ-ViT across multiple architectures and tasks, particularly under low-bit quantization. The code is available at https://github.com/Runqing-forMost/rankq-vit.git

title: Multi-Node Transformers for Object Detection and Captioning Across Distributed Edge Networks
abstract: This paper presents a unified transformer-based framework for object detection and dense region captioning across distributed edge networks. The architecture uses a shared visual encoder followed by detection, region extraction, and autoregressive language-decoding stages, allowing localization and region description to reuse the same image features. This design removes the second image-encoding path required by decoupled detection and captioning pipelines. To support execution on resource-limited devices, a workload-allocation formulation assigns model stages and input streams across connected edge nodes while accounting for execution time, memory capacity, processor utilization, power limits, and intermediate tensor transfer cost. The framework is evaluated on a six-device edge testbed comprising four NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Orin NX inference nodes and two Raspberry Pi 5 auxiliary CPU nodes, with TensorRT FP16 and INT8 execution on the NVIDIA devices. On a Jetson Orin Nano, the unified INT8 model achieves 38.1 FPS with 3.5 GB peak memory use and 11.8 W measured power. Under four concurrent streams, the proposed allocation achieves 35.2 FPS and 28.4 ms mean end-to-end latency with an internode transfer rate of 6.8 MB/s.

title: BiRefNet-V2: Rethinking Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation
abstract: Dichotomous image segmentation requires pixel-accurate foreground-background separation while preserving fine structures such as thin filaments, sharp edges, and intricate textures. BiRefNet addressed this challenge through bilateral references, combining image patches and gradient information, but its inward reference loses local spatial structure and lacks semantic guidance, while its outward reference relies on single-channel gradient attention. We recast this paradigm as controlled information recovery - locality determines what spatial information survives, semantic selectivity what information enters, and focused boundary supervision where refinement occurs - and propose BiRefNet-V2 to implement it: (1) locality-preserving and semantically guided detail injection through space-to-depth transformation, overlapping patches, and a Semantically Guided Gate; (2) a learned boundary stream with focused supervision that generates full-channel residual attention without requiring boundary annotations; and (3) a dual-branch decoder integrating depth-wise boundary convolutions with large-kernel attention. A modernized framework - LayerNorm, GELU, the Lion optimizer, and a DINOv3 backbone - cuts training from 600 to 50 epochs. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on DIS5K, camouflaged object detection, and high-resolution salient object detection across all 13 evaluation sets. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet-V2.

title: Differentiable Virtual-Slot Partitioning for Adaptive Tokenization in Vision Transformers
abstract: Adaptive tokenization aims to reduce the compute spent on uninformative image regions while preserving accuracy. Existing work relies on (i) fixed or frozen scoring rules, which cannot be trained toward the task loss, or (ii) discrete masks trained with straight-through estimators, which yield noisy gradients, while fully differentiable alternatives instead leave the pre-trained regular grid. We revisit adaptive tokenization from a regular-grid perspective and ask: can a two-scale quadtree be learned end-to-end without deleting a single token during training? We show that one coarse token and its four fine children can be made the two endpoints of a single continuous interpolation. We introduce Differentiable Virtual-Slot Partitioning (\dvsp{}), which keeps four \emph{virtual slots} per $2{\times}2$ region and blends their token features and attention mass with a single weight $α$, exactly reproducing the discrete grid at $α\in \{0,1\}$. On COCO detection with EVA-02-B, \dvsp{} retains $97.9\%$ of dense Box AP while removing $64.2\%$ of visual tokens, giving a $1.61\times$ end-to-end speedup, and it outperforms entropy-based APT, DART, and uniform lower-resolution dense adaptation at matched budgets; these gains depend on the conserved attention mass, whose removal costs $1.59$ Box AP. On a frozen Segmenter it also improves Cityscapes mIoU, and on frozen DeiT backbones it exceeds entropy selection at identical per-image token counts.

title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: My Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge
abstract: The CoRL 2026 RoboEval challenge has eight bimanual tasks, and it ranks a policy not only on whether it succeeds but on how: every stage of the task, done safely, efficiently and with both arms in coordination, scored against human demonstrations. My solution has two parts. The generic part, carried over from my LeHome challenge solution, is off-policy RL on a $π_{0.5}$-based policy that is also its own value function. It is trained with AWR and RECAP on advantages of the exact official score, in a loop where every rollout is at the same time a Thompson-sampling trial of about 20 inference parameters. Out of the box, it took the policy to 0.85 RDS on held-out seeds in two days (and it was still very far from convergence). The competition-specific part adds data that local exploration cannot find: generated demonstrations that reach the full reward, and recovery episodes that start from the policy's own failures. The submitted policy reaches 0.990 RDS on held-out seeds and 0.987 on the official seeds.
